brief: a pre-registered study by a domain expert (`prereg.json`, a JSON object; no code runs). Each agent is an expert in one field (descriptor mechanism = field, method = study_type) and must do real research first: read papers via the swarm's Exa leads, then register BEFORE seeing data: {field, study_type, question, hypothesis, mechanism (why the effect should exist), citations (>= 2 Exa source ids S<k> or URLs from this run's research, or sources.json), dataset: {url of a real public CSV/TSV (open-data host such as raw.githubusercontent.com, zenodo, figshare, OSF, Dryad, data.gov, Rdatasets, or a URL in the Exa results), x, x_level, y, y_level (exact column header text; level = the answer compared vs everyone else, omit for numeric columns)}, direction (positive|negative), predicted_rho (expected |Spearman rho|)}. The host verifies citations, downloads the data once, and runs the registered test ONCE on all rows (Spearman, p < 0.005, matching sign; one test per dataset per run, so a second registration on a used dataset scores 0). Trivial pairs (same column, near-identical wording, two demographics) score 0. loss = 1 - (replicated and significant): significant = the registered test gives p < 0.005 on all rows with the registered sign; replicated = the same sign with p < 0.05 in each of the two fixed hash halves of the rows. Every study is logged for a post-run Ig Nobel committee (two LLM judges, laugh and think), which does not affect the loss. If a column name is wrong the run fails and lists the dataset's usable columns. The baseline registration (rare-steak eaters smoke more) is a real hypothesis that fails (loss 1); aim for a real, odd, everyday effect that makes people laugh, then think
proxy_note: pre-registered confirmatory test on real public data; Ig Nobel committee runs after the run (score_run.py)

scout.goal: a real, odd, everyday phenomenon (human, animal, food or object behaviour) that is documented in published research or open data the swarm has NOT used yet, ideally with a downloadable raw CSV/TSV
scout.channels: paper_query: search papers and past Ig Nobel winners for a measurable everyday oddity. code_query: search for a raw, downloadable CSV/TSV dataset on that oddity (GitHub raw files, Zenodo, figshare, OSF, Dryad, data.gov).
scout.pick_criterion: points to real data (ideally a direct CSV/TSV URL) or a real published effect the study can test on the existing surveys
scout.extract_question: Give any direct CSV/TSV download URL for the data, what each column measures, the sample size, and the headline finding (effect size, p-value).
